A2_Scope.description: This chapter defines the axiomatic and operational structure of the Willingness function in the Behavioral Change Model (BCM 2.0/BEATRIX). It specifies determinants, conditions, and modulation mechanisms of Willingness as the central switching point for behavioral change and architecture development. The module is mandatory for all simulations, modelings, and interventions that represent Willingness as trigger or barrier.

goals: Formalization of Willingness as a decision criterion for behavioral change
Operationalization and measurability of Willingness in individuals, groups, and organizations
Integration of the Willingness function with utility structures, awareness, context, and segment logic
Ensuring transparency and comparability for simulations and intervention architectures

A4_Axioms.name: Willingness as a Threshold Function
A4_Axioms.definition: Willingness emerges when the subjective total utility exceeds the individual decision threshold.

A4_Axioms.name: Utility Integration
A4_Axioms.definition: Willingness is based on a weighted integration of individual, collective, and identity-related utility components.
A4_Axioms.formal: N_total(t) = ω_ind * N_ind(t) + ω_kol * N_kol(t) + ω_id * N_id(t)

A4_Axioms.name: Awareness as a Necessary Condition
A4_Axioms.definition: Without activated awareness, no Willingness can emerge.

A4_Axioms.name: Context Dependence
A4_Axioms.definition: Willingness is modulated by situational context factors C(t).

A4_Axioms.name: Segment Dependence
A4_Axioms.definition: Each segment has its own threshold and weighting parameters.
A4_Axioms.notes: Segment parameterization must be consistent with the active segmentation grid (e.g., BCM2_09_SEG).

A4_Axioms.name: Dynamics
A4_Axioms.definition: Willingness is time-dependent and can change through learning, experience, and feedback.

A4_Axioms.name: Social Reinforcement
A4_Axioms.definition: Willingness is influenced by social norms and observed behavior of others.

A4_Axioms.name: Uncertainty and Risk
A4_Axioms.definition: Risk and uncertainty perception modulate the Willingness threshold.

A4_Axioms.name: Cognitive and Emotional Moderation
A4_Axioms.definition: Individual cognitive and emotional factors act as amplifiers or blockers.

A4_Axioms.name: Measurability
A4_Axioms.definition: Willingness can be operationalized via observable indicators and experimental designs.

non_normative_axioms.name: Dynamic Complementarity
non_normative_axioms.definition: The Willingness function is dynamic and does not arise from the utility types (INU, KNU, IDN) alone, but in complementarity with the awareness function, the context vector, and the Behavioral Change Journey. These three dimensions determine which utilities are salient, how they are modulated, and how willingness evolves over time.

formal.core: W(t) = f(N_ind_eff(t), N_kol_eff(t), N_id_eff(t), AWX(t), KON(t), JNY(t))
interpretation: Awareness (AWX) selects and modulates salience (hyper, blockade, neutral).
Context (KON) defines situational triggers and weightings.
Journey (JNY) models temporal sequences (build-up, reinforcement, decay, forgetting).

non_normative_axioms.name: Awareness Boundary States and Complementarity Binding
non_normative_axioms.definition: The Willingness function is subject to boundary states of awareness complementarity. In awareness blockade (A_mod(t)=0), willingness is fully suppressed regardless of utility. In hyper-awareness (A_mod(t) ≫ θ), willingness is disproportionately amplified even under low or negative individual utility. All modulations through awareness, context, and journey are formally bound to the complementarity axioms (K1–K10, K12).

formal.piecewise: W(t) = { 0 if A_mod(t) = 0; f(N_i_eff(t)) ↑↑ if A_mod(t) ≫ θ; f(N_i_eff(t)) otherwise }
formal.binding: κ_AWX,i, κ_KON,i, κ_JNY,i are constrained by the complementarity axiom frame (K-axioms / 7240).

non_normative_axioms.name: Transition to Probabilities
non_normative_axioms.definition: Willingness is the necessary and sufficient input variable for the probability function. Transition probabilities between states or behavioral phases arise exclusively from dynamic Willingness and are modulated by thresholds, segments, journey parameters, and context.

formal.core: P(i→j, t) = g(W(t), θ_W,S, α_JNY(t), C(t))
edge_cases: If W(t) < θ_W,S then P(i→j, t) = 0
If W(t) → ∞ then P(i→j, t) → 1 (asymptotic; never exactly 100%)
formal.bridge: Explicit bridge from BCM2_06_KOM7259 (Willingness) to probability/transition modules (e.g., PRB/WTX family).

requirements: Loaded modules for utility functions (BCM2_01_INU, BCM2_02_KNU, BCM2_03_IDN), awareness (BCM2_05_AWX), segment logic (BCM2_08_PRB / BCM2_09_SEG)
Context vector defined for each application

integration: Direct coupling to utility functions, awareness, segment logic, and the Behavioral Change Journey (BCM2_10_JNY)
Integration into the intervention toolkit (BCM2_13_INT) and agent-based simulations

constraints: Only BCM-conform terminology is used (no psychological, suggestive, or system-external wording)
No use for individual diagnostics; only for architecture-based change and intervention processes

literature: Empirical studies on willingness in field and lab experiments

Commercial and scientific use requires written permission from FehrAdvice & Partners AG

summary: Formally precise, operationalizable steering and simulation of behavioral change
Integration of utility, awareness, context, and segment logics
Practical derivation of interventions and measurements
Maximum transparency and auditability for organization, research, and policy
